findings.problem: SampleWorkflow uses a status: String field alongside is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool, and sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> lifecycle booleans, allowing illegal state combinations such as status="sent" with is_sent=false, is_validated=false with is_sent=true, or sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(0) with is_sent=false. The compiler cannot enforce any lifecycle invariant.
findings.failure_mode: Business logic can observe or persist contradictory lifecycle state (e.g., item appears sent but sent_at_epoch_ms is None, or item is marked sent without being validated). Any caller reading these fields must manually reconcile them, and bugs compound across the system.
findings.fix: Replace status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool, sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> with a single enum typestate (e.g., enum WorkflowState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }) and make SampleWorkflow a newtype wrapping it. Use a fallible constructor to prevent illegal transitions.

findings.problem: status: String is a raw primitive with no domain constraints. Any string value is valid, including "sent", "SENT", "", "deleted", or "sent_pending". There is no typed domain error for invalid status transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Typos, external input, or internal bugs can put the workflow into an undefined status string. Downstream code comparing status == "sent" is fragile and must check equality of arbitrary strings instead of exhaustively matching enum variants.
findings.fix: Define a non-exhaustive enum (e.g., pub enum WorkflowStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent, Failed }) and use it instead of String. Replace mark_sent with a typed method that returns a Result wrapping a domain error for invalid transitions.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are lifecycle booleans that encode the same semantic information as status. This duplication means the booleans and status string can diverge (e.g., is_sent=true but status="pending"). The skill explicitly requires replacing bool lifecycle flags with enums or typestates.
findings.failure_mode: Mutations that update one field but not the other create inconsistent state. Any new boolean flag added (is_deleted, is_archived) compounds the inconsistency problem.
findings.fix: Remove is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms. Encode them in a single typestate enum. If additional lifecycle phases are needed, extend the enum—not add more booleans.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes SampleWorkflow by value and unconditionally sets status="sent", is_sent=true without any precondition checks. It can mark an item as sent even if it was not validated, even if it is already sent, and without recording sent_at_epoch_ms. Returns SampleWorkflow instead of Result<SampleWorkflow, _>.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid transitions execute silently. The item can be sent without validation, sent twice (double-send), or sent without a timestamp. Callers have no way to detect or handle rejected transitions.
findings.fix: Change signature to pub fn mark_sent(item: SampleWorkflow) -> Result<SampleWorkflow, WorkflowError>. Add preconditions: status must be Validated (or equivalent typestate variant), not already Sent. Set sent_at_epoch_ms = current_epoch() and return a typed WorkflowError::InvalidTransition for rejected calls.

findings.problem: All fields of SampleWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to directly mutate status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms without going through any domain method or constructor.
findings.failure_mode: External callers can create illegal states at any point in the lifecycle (e.g., directly setting is_sent=true without calling mark_sent), bypassing all domain invariants.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (remove pub). Expose only read-only accessors or methods as needed. Provide a fallible constructor or builder that enforces invariants at construction time.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no return type indicating failure. There is no WorkflowError (or similar) enum for domain errors like InvalidTransition, AlreadySent, or NotValidated. The function silently mutates state rather than returning a Result.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid transitions are swallowed. The caller cannot distinguish a successful transition from a no-op or an error, leading to silent data corruption or lost business events.
findings.fix: Define a domain error enum: pub enum WorkflowError { InvalidTransition, AlreadySent, NotValidated }. Change mark_sent to return Result<SampleWorkflow, WorkflowError>. Enforce preconditions before mutation.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> exists but mark_sent never sets it. There is no clock abstraction or current_epoch() function to provide the timestamp. This is an imperative-shell concern (clock access) that should be injected or called at the boundary.
findings.failure_mode: Sent items have no recorded timestamp, breaking audit trails, SLA tracking, and downstream consumers that rely on sent_at_epoch_ms for ordering or latency calculations.
findings.fix: Add a current_epoch_ms() fn (or clock trait) and call it inside mark_sent to populate sent_at_epoch_ms. Gate clock access behind the imperative shell boundary.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain constraints. There is no WorkflowId newtype to prevent confusing this with other string IDs (user ID, session ID, etc.).
findings.failure_mode: IDs can be accidentally mixed up between domain entities. No format validation (length, charset) is enforced at the type level.
findings.fix: Define pub struct WorkflowId(String) with a smart constructor that validates format. Use WorkflowId as the id field type.

residual_risk: Static review only with no commands run and no test files present. The crate has fundamental typestate violations that make illegal states fully representable. Without enum-based typestate, domain error types, and private fields, the workflow can enter and persist in any contradictory state combination. The single function mark_sent has no preconditions, no error signaling, and omits setting sent_at_epoch_ms.
